haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler, or the retry timer 15 minutes after a failed attempt. It extracts replica orders with updated_at > hwm minus 2h and updated_at <= cutoff.
haiku-low.q2: updated_at is set when each row is written, not when the bulk import commits. The row can appear on the replica up to 90 minutes after that updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The edit sets updated_at, so a later nightly extract whose window covers it picks it up. The MERGE overwrites the warehouse row only if the incoming updated_at is newer.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which also sets updated_at. The merge sets is_deleted = true. Rows are never removed from the warehouse.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt rolls back, hwm is unchanged, and its run_log row is set to failed. Attempt 1 or 2 retries 15 minutes later. Attempt 3 pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 and show the last committed night, consistent but stale. A staleness alert goes to #data-alerts, even if on-call was already paged.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day, up to night_cutoff, and reloads a mismatched day from the replica if its creation day is in the last 30 days.
haiku-low.q8: MERGE overwrites only when the incoming updated_at is newer, so stale or duplicate copies match nothing new. Staging keeps one row per order_id with the greatest updated_at.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in ops.pipeline_state as hwm. It is set to the cutoff, the clock time read before the replica query, inside the same transaction that commits the merge.
haiku-low.q10: The MERGE, the hwm update and the run_log status commit in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards read only analytics.orders, so they see the old night or the new one whole.
haiku-low.q11: Staged rows from the failed attempt are deleted when the next attempt starts for that run_date. The retry extracts updated_at > hwm minus 2h up to a new cutoff.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that creation day from the replica, with updated_at <= night_cutoff, stages it, and MERGEs with the same guard in the day's own transaction. It does not move the HWM.

sonnet.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler (or the retry timer 15 min after a failed attempt, or a manual rerun) starts it. It extracts every replica `orders` row with updated_at > hwm - 2h and updated_at <= cutoff.
sonnet.q2: A bulk import can stay open up to 90 minutes, and each row gets updated_at when written, not at commit. So the row can appear in the replica up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at; a later nightly extract (window from hwm - 2h to cutoff) picks it up and the MERGE overwrites the warehouse row because the incoming updated_at is newer.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (soft delete), which also sets updated_at. The load treats it like any write: the row is updated and is_deleted = true. Rows are never removed from the warehouse.
sonnet.q5: The transaction rolls back, run_log status is set to failed, and HWM is unchanged. If failed attempts for the run_date are 1 or 2, a retry timer starts the next attempt 15 min later. If the count is 3, on-call is paged. The 60-minute deadline also counts as failure.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh anyway and show the last committed night (consistent but stale). A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel (even if on-call was already paged).
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation: it compares each creation day in the last 30 days (count and checksum) with the replica, finds the mismatch, and reloads that day (if the Sunday night committed).
sonnet.q8: Staging keeps only the greatest-updated_at row per order_id, and the MERGE only updates an existing order if the incoming updated_at is newer (stale or equal copies leave it alone), so re-running matches nothing new.
sonnet.q9: In ops.pipeline_state (column hwm). It is set to the cutoff (the job clock time read before the replica query), not max(updated_at), inside the same warehouse transaction as the MERGE, just before COMMIT.
sonnet.q10: The MERGE, the HWM update and the run_log committed status happen in one warehouse transaction that commits together or not at all. Dashboards read only analytics.orders, never staging, so they see the whole previous night or the whole new one. If the warehouse can't isolate this, a shadow table swapped in atomically is the fallback.
sonnet.q11: The failed attempt's staged rows are deleted at the start of the next attempt for the same run_date. The retry re-extracts the same window, since HWM is unchanged (updated_at > hwm - 2h and <= a new cutoff).
sonnet.q12: It re-extracts from the replica that creation day's rows with updated_at at or before night_cutoff, writes them to staging, and applies them with the same guarded MERGE in the day's own transaction. It does not move the HWM.
